## Pull in compiled DOC_Nutr_SO4_Cl_H2S_pH data and export annual files
```{r Pull in compiled data files, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}

#write out a csv of all the data to the main folder: 
final_data <- read.csv("../COMPASS_TEMPEST_AllData_AllYears.csv")

##Remove the old annual folders
unlink("Data package/2022", recursive = TRUE)
unlink("Data package/2023", recursive = TRUE)
unlink("Data package/2024", recursive = TRUE)
unlink("Data package/2025", recursive = TRUE)

##Files in annual folders
dir.create("Data package/2022")
dir.create("Data package/2023")
dir.create("Data package/2024")
dir.create("Data package/2025")

##Separate by year for ESS-DIVE 
final_data_2022 <- subset(final_data, Sample_Year == "2022")
final_data_2023 <- subset(final_data, Sample_Year == "2023")
final_data_2024 <- subset(final_data, Sample_Year == "2024")
final_data_2025 <- subset(final_data, Sample_Year == "2025")

##Write out annual data files
write.csv(final_data_2022, "Data package/2022/COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_DOC_Nutr_SO4_Cl_H2S_pH_2022.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(final_data_2023, "Data package/2023/COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_DOC_Nutr_SO4_Cl_H2S_pH_2023.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(final_data_2024, "Data package/2024/COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_DOC_Nutr_SO4_Cl_H2S_pH_2024.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(final_data_2025, "Data package/2025/COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_DOC_Nutr_SO4_Cl_H2S_pH_2025.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

## Create flmd file
```{r create flmd}

files  = list.files("Data package", recursive = TRUE)
files

files = c("COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_analysis_2022.csv", "COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_analysis_2023.csv", "COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_analysis_2024.csv","COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_analysis_2025.csv", "dd.csv")

flmd <- data.frame(file_name = files)
flmd

flmd$file_description <- ""
flmd$standard <- ""
flmd$file_version <- ""
flmd$data_orientation <- ""
flmd$header_rows <- ""
flmd$column_or_row_name_position <- ""
flmd$notes <- ""

#add information about each line:

flmd$file_description <-  c("Porewater, sourcewater, and rainwater samples collected from COMPASS TEMPEST site in 2022",
                            "Porewater, sourcewater, and rainwater samples collected from COMPASS TEMPEST site in 2023",
                            "Porewater, sourcewater, and rainwater samples collected from COMPASS TEMPEST site in 2024",
                            "Porewater, sourcewater, and rainwater samples collected from COMPASS TEMPEST site in 2025",
                            "Data dictionary file for annual TEMPEST water sample analysis data files describing each column in the dataset")

flmd$data_orientation <-  c("horizontal",
                            "horizontal",
                            "horizontal",
                            "horizontal",
                            "horizontal")

flmd$header_rows <-   c("1",
                        "1",
                        "1",
                        "1",
                        "1")

flmd$column_or_row_name_position <- c("1",
                                      "1",
                                      "1",
                                      "1",
                                      "1")


#write out the flmd associated with the data:
write.csv(flmd, "Data package/flmd.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```


## Create site list - can we use the site list from the sensor data publications? 
```{#r create site list}

##Description, Latitude, Longitude

TMP <- data.frame(
Description = "Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatments (TEMPEST) experimental site; This manipulative, ecosystem-scale TEMPEST experiment addresses the potential for freshwater and estuarine-water disturbance events to alter tree function, species composition, and ecosystem processes in a deciduous coastal forest in MD, USA. The experiment uses a large-unit (2000 m2), un-replicated experimental design, with three 50 m × 40 m plots serving as control, freshwater, and estuarine-water treatments. The TEMPEST experiment is in a mid- to late-successional (~80 years old) temperate, deciduous coastal forest.
Latitude: 
Longitude: )

site_list = TMP

#write out the site list associated with the data:
write.csv(site_list, "Data package/site_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```


## Data Description - NEED TO EDIT THIS
```{r data description}

#Create a text file that has the description of the data - This ideally should match the text that is in the data READ.ME 

datadescription <- "These data are measurements of porewater and source water samples collected in 2022-2025 from the COMPASS TEMPEST site in the Chesapeake Bay region in three experimental plots: Saltwater Treatment (S), Freshwater Treatment (F), and Control (C). Porewater was collected from lysimeters at 15, 30, and 50 cm depths semi-monthly from 2022-2025, and 1-2 times per day during flooding events. Porewater samples were pulled from lysimeters using an extraction kit consisting of a syringe and tubing, and source water samples were collected from a barge on the nearby estuary (estuary source water samples) or from the emitter lines (F and S source water samples). These samples were then aliquoted into bottles for analysis of sulfate, chloride, sulfide, nutrient, and dissolved organic carbon concentrations. Samples were analyzed for pH, conductivity, and temperature at the time of sample collection. Analysis of each constituent is described in the data dictionary and further details, including quality assurance and quality control for all analyses can be found on the COMPASS TEMPEST Porewater page (https://github.com/COMPASS-DOE/TEMPEST_Porewater)"

##Add something about how rainwater was collected? 

#write to a text file 
writeLines(datadescription, "Data package/COMPASS_TEMPEST_water_analysis_DataDescription.txt")


```


## Create Author List - NEED TO EDIT THIS 
```{#r create author list}

#Pull in the common synoptic authors list: 
authors_common <- read.csv(here("Metadata/Synoptic CB/", "COMPASS_SynopticCB_common_essdive_author_list.csv"))


#create a list of the last names you want to pull 
names_we_want <- c("Wilson", "Read", "Stearns", "Phillips", "Chin", "Megonigal")

#Subset the common list for the names that we want 
author_list <- authors_common %>%
  filter(last_name %in% names_we_want)

#if you need to add any other authors 
others <- data.frame(
  first_name = c("first_name1", "first_name2"), 
  last_name = c("last_name1", "last_name2"), 
  orcid = c("orcid_id1", "orcid_id2"), 
  affiliation = c("affiliation1", "affiliation2"), 
  email = c("email1", "email2")
)

#add in the other authors

#write out the author list associated with the data:
```
